## 2.10.0 (2026-11-27)

### Summary

Version 2.10.0 bundles a new managed skill, vvoc-project-session-history, which recaps recent project work from OpenCode's local session database, and adds flat scripts/ delivery support so the skill's extractor is installed and kept up to date during install and sync. Both that extractor and the vv-reflect session-graph pre-pass now read the post-migration session_part store, restoring assistant messages, changed-file lists, and tool/file counts for the newest sessions instead of reporting empty recaps, while inline content still wins so older and transition-era sessions stay unchanged. The session-history skill's routing description was rewritten into a single clear English trigger line with the usage-analytics exclusion, and new tests pin archive call-id precedence and inline-wins behavior. A workflow fix (issue #43) releases a checkpoint reviewer binding that is provably dead after a transport-level launch failure, so a stuck review slot can be relaunched instead of blocking verify, recover, and start forever, while live and completed reviews still reject relaunches as before.

* test(vv-reflect): pin archive precedence and tree inline-wins with discriminating fixtures ([a02515c](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/a02515c)), closes [#64](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/issues/64)
* fix(managed-skills): read session_part so new sessions keep assistant messages ([4e088b3](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/4e088b3))
* fix(managed-skills): reduce the session-history description to pure routing triggers ([501e73c](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/501e73c))
* fix(managed-skills): rewrite the session-history skill description, drop Russian text ([413bc4a](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/413bc4a))
* fix(vv-reflect): read session_part so reflection sees post-migration sessions ([2b7fe2a](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/2b7fe2a))
* fix(workflow): release a provably dead checkpoint reviewer binding ([c62d5c0](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/c62d5c0)), closes [#43](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/issues/43)
* feat(managed-skills): bundle project-session recap skill with scripts/ delivery ([8181b0d](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/8181b0d))

## 2.9.0 (2026-11-25)

### Summary

Version 2.9.0 removes session-wide orchestration profiles (single-session, balanced, orchestrated, and delegated) as a public CLI, config, preset, and session-settings choice, so execution behavior is now driven by the request or selected plan instead of a session-wide policy that could also shift the cached request prefix. Legacy vvoc.json files carrying root or per-preset orchestration sections are migrated by `vvoc sync`, which removes those sections from both project and global configs with a timestamped backup and a change report before strict validation, while other documents that still contain orchestration now fail loudly. Families without a recorded profile receive a stable `work_policy_default` section in the managed controller prompt, legacy families keep their frozen tail policy, the `vvoc orchestration` command and `/vv-settings` profile action are gone, and `/context` now accepts profile-less records. This is a breaking change for anyone relying on the removed profiles or the deleted command.

* fix(orchestration): close review findings on migration coverage and projections ([28d7769](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/28d7769))
* feat(orchestration)!: remove session-wide orchestration profiles ([77145bd](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/77145bd))

## 2.8.0 (2026-11-24)

### Summary

Version 2.8.0 standardizes all eleven managed skills on a canonical six-block grammar with scope, workflow, rules, and done blocks plus optional artifact and refs sections, removing the old universal root, identity, and task envelopes while preserving the skills' existing obligations. It also unifies the VV-plan and VV-execute execution vocabulary, restores English-output rules and lifecycle guidance, adds contents sections to long references, and introduces a deterministic grammar and reference gate that rejects malformed structures such as nested or uppercase elements, unterminated CDATA, and missing or poorly placed contents. These changes give users more consistent, predictable skill prompts and stronger validation that installed skills remain well-formed.

* fix(skills): restore preserved obligations and harden grammar gate ([135285e](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/135285e))
* feat(skills): adopt canonical six-block grammar for managed skills ([0bb0e0a](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode/commit/0bb0e0a))

## <small>2.7.1 (2026-11-24)</small>

### Summary

Version 2.7.1 expands the bundled managed skills that guide day-to-day work. A new vv-verification skill adds one language-agnostic decision workflow with six on-demand references covering strategy, oracles, evidence, formal methods, maintenance, and bootstrapping a project verification stack, while vv-spec and vv-plan now ask for verification intent inside their existing fields so plans name the property and oracle behind each criterion. Two new writing skills, vv-write-for-humans for reader-facing prose and vv-write-for-agents for agent-executed instructions, are hardened with clearer trigger wording and tighter content, banned-token, and volume gates so they install predictably. The design-guidance skill is renamed from vv-design-principles to vv-ui-design-principles, so anyone invoking the old name should switch to the new one. Install and sync test expectations are now derived from the skill registry, keeping counts accurate as skills are added, and the guidance docs gained a rule against piping gate commands without pipefail plus a pinned reviewer prompt shape.

## 2.7.0 (2026-11-24)

### Summary

Version 2.7.0 adds the vv-design-principles managed skill, giving agents a build-and-audit design process for web and app UI: it plans design tokens before writing code, enforces a measurable quality floor, runs a subtractive audit against a catalog of generic design tells, and anchors decisions in a project DESIGN.md design-system file, with the tell catalog, quality-floor numbers, and DESIGN.md contract loaded on demand from three bundled references. The skill is registered in the managed-skill list so vvoc install and sync ship it and doctor can report drift, and it is documented in the README as an additive companion to existing design skills. The release also tightens DESIGN.md discovery so it stays within the current package, reorganizes and clarifies several catalog entries for more accurate guidance, and improves the quality-floor verification steps to distinguish what was actually checked from what still needs confirmation.

issues.title: workflow: revertInFlightDelegatedLaunches is dead code — delegated attempts orphaned by a host crash stay in_flight forever (ATTEMPT_IN_FLIGHT, no recover path)
runtime: family-snapshot admission rejects its own first-work model switch — bare sessions whose creation model differs from roles.default die on first dispatch (SnapshotAdmissionError, 2.4.0)
workflow: a checkpoint reviewer launch that dies at transport permanently binds the generation slot (ALREADY_LAUNCHED deadlock, no recover path)
vv-plan/vv-spec: XML-authoring hazards undocumented; the lint accepts malformed XML that a strict parser rejects; self-review lacks a contract-fidelity check
